y-m-44-01.topic: Set of points equally distant from two points (perpendicular bisector of a segment)
y-m-44-01.goal: Find points manually to check points equally far from two points no be one point but line; explain with equations why dem form line.
y-m-44-01.material: Two sea harbors. On coordinate plane (1 square=1 km), A=(0,0), B=(6,2). To make rescue boat same distance from either harbor in emergency, station it at a point equally distant from both. 1 1 0 0 6 2
y-m-44-01.thinking.2: Separate a few examples from general reason
y-m-44-01.prereq.0: School sequence note: H1 here only production difficulty, not fixed grade. Assume learner studied equations of figures (lines, circles) in high-school Common Mathematics.
y-m-44-01.prereq.1: Prior knowledge: distance between points on coordinate plane; set expressions equal and expand.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.prompt: Suppose mark every sea point same distance from harbors A and B. Together, what shape those points make?
y-m-44-01.s.s1.hint.0: Choose point other than segment AB midpoint (3,1), write distance to A and B. (Example: (2,4)) 3 1 2 4
y-m-44-01.s.s1.hint.1: Find 3 or 4 points, plot them on coordinate plane, and see which shape they line up on.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.o.a: Only midpoint of AB, no other point.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.r.a: Midpoint is only one equidistant point. Choose another and compare distances to A,B.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.o.b: Circle centered at A through B.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.r.b: Points on circle are only same distance from A; here distances to A and B must equal.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.o.c: One line through midpoint of AB.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.r.c: Test prediction by plotting points and seeing their shape.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.o.d: A line through harbors A and B.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.r.d: Points on AB often closer to one harbor; compare distances at sample points.
y-m-44-01.s.s1.explain: Equidistant points include midpoint (3,1) and distant (2,4). They lie on perpendicular bisector through midpoint. Prediction for now; next find points to check. [3 1 2 4]
y-m-44-01.s.s2.prompt: On coordinate plane east=x, north=y. A(0,0), B(6,2), 1 square=1 km. Place rescue boat at lattice point (integer x,y), sea x,y≥0, equal distance from A,B, within 10 km of A. Find 3 spots. [0 0 6 2 1 1 0 0 10 3]
y-m-44-01.s.s2.hint.0: For a chosen point, separately calculate squared distances to A x²+y² and B; compare.
y-m-44-01.s.s2.hint.1: Fix x=0,1,2,... then vary y to find equality. [0 1 2]
y-m-44-01.s.s2.ok.c3: Same distance from A and B.
y-m-44-01.s.s2.explain: Four lattice points fit: (3,1),(2,4),(1,7),(0,10). They follow y decreases 3 for each x increase 1. (4,−2) outside sea, exclude. [3 1 2 4 1 7 0 10 3 1 4 2]
y-m-44-01.s.s3.prompt: Your points lie on a line, but few points do not prove all do. Explain why equal-distance condition becomes line in x,y.
y-m-44-01.s.s3.hint.0: For P(x,y), equate squared distances to A and B.
y-m-44-01.s.s3.hint.1: Expand and see terms on both sides.
y-m-44-01.s.s3.placeholder: Example: “distance to A equals distance to B” as equation gives ...
y-m-44-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you distinguish points appearing lined up from simplified equation being a line?
y-m-44-01.s.s3.model.0: P equidistant: PA²=PB², x²+y²=(x−6)²+(y−2)². Expanding cancels x²,y², leaves first-degree relation such as 3x+y=10, a line. [6 2 3 10]
y-m-44-01.s.s3.model.1: Four points aligned is example, not proof. Squaring equal-distance condition cancels x²,y² and leaves first-degree equation, so it is a line.
y-m-44-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: Answer expressing same idea in another order.

y-m-44-06.title: Booth next to fountain: spot on boundary allowed?
y-m-44-06.topic: Points inside region wey circle and line define (inequality regions, whether boundary included)
y-m-44-06.goal: For region given by circle and line inequalities, check separately for each condition whether boundary included, make some points wey meet conditions, explain effect of changing one condition.
y-m-44-06.material: Park map on coordinate plane (1 square=10 m). Fountain at (2,1), possible booth places na lattice points meeting all 3 conditions. ㈎ Distance from fountain no more than 4 (boundary included): (x−2)²+(y−1)²≤16. ㈏ Above line y=x−5, meaning y>x−5 (spot on line na walkway, no booth allowed). ㈐ x≥0. 1 10 2 1 4 2 1 16 5 5 0
y-m-44-06.thinking.0: Check conditions separately, one by one
y-m-44-06.thinking.2: Predict effect of changing a condition
y-m-44-06.prereq.1: Prior knowledge: regions shown by circle and line inequalities (inside/outside, above/below).
y-m-44-06.s.s1.prompt: Student wan decide if booth fit set at (6,1). Choose best judgment. 6 1
y-m-44-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write ㈎, ㈏, ㈐ one by one and make table with ○ and × to show whether (6,1) meet each. 6 1
y-m-44-06.s.s1.hint.1: Find which condition get point on boundary, then check wording whether condition include boundary.
y-m-44-06.s.s1.o.a: Booth fit set: distance from fountain exactly 4 (circle boundary), and boundary included, so allowed
y-m-44-06.s.s1.r.a: You only check circle condition. You gats check line condition ㈏ too.
y-m-44-06.s.s1.o.b: Booth no fit set: e meet ㈎ but dey on line y=x−5, so fail ㈏
y-m-44-06.s.s1.r.b: You check all three separately and judge failing one mean no. You see boundary inclusion differ by condition.
y-m-44-06.s.s1.o.c: Booth no fit set: distance from fountain na 4, so e no meet 'no more than 4'
y-m-44-06.s.s1.r.c: 'No more than' include 4 too. Read condition wording again.
y-m-44-06.s.s1.o.d: No fit tell: problem no say if boundary points included
y-m-44-06.s.s1.r.d: Problem state for each condition whether boundary included. Read condition text again.
y-m-44-06.s.s1.explain: (6,1) distance 4 from fountain (2,1), so meet ㈎ (boundary included). But put into y=x−5 gives 1=6−5, so e dey on line and ㈏ say spot on line excluded. Boundary treated differently for each condition, so check separately. 6 1 4 2 1 5 1 6 5
y-m-44-06.s.s2.prompt: Make possible booth spots by entering 4 different lattice points (integer x and y) wey meet all ㈎, ㈏, ㈐.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.hint.0: Fix one x first and find y range wey meet ㈎.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.hint.1: From that range, cross out y values wey no meet ㈏ and choose among rest.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.ok.c2: ㈎ Distance from fountain no more than 4.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.fail.c2: E no meet ㈎. Check whether square of distance from fountain (2,1) no more than 16. 2 1 16
y-m-44-06.s.s2.fail.c3: E no meet ㈏. Point on line no allowed; e gats dey above line.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.fail.c4: E no meet ㈐. x gats be at least 0.
y-m-44-06.s.s2.explain: 36 lattice points meet conditions altogether. Plenty answers possible, e.g. (2,1), (3,2), (0,1), (2,4). (6,1) left out because on line; (6,3) because distance from fountain √20>4; (−1,1) because x<0. 36 2 1 3 2 0 1 2 4 6 1 6 3 20 4 −1 1 0
y-m-44-06.s.s3.prompt: Suppose later dem change condition ㈎ from 'no more than 4' to 'less than 4' (boundary excluded). Check whether any points you just enter change; if yes, explain which and why; if no, explain why not.
y-m-44-06.s.s3.hint.0: Write square of distance from fountain for each point and compare with 16.
y-m-44-06.s.s3.hint.1: Compare result for 'no more than' and 'less than' when value exactly 16.
y-m-44-06.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Among my points, ... distance from fountain ..., so ...
y-m-44-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You check whether any point exactly 4 away from fountain?
y-m-44-06.s.s3.selfAssess.1: If none, you too write why none dey?
y-m-44-06.s.s3.model.0: My point (2,5) exactly 4 away from fountain (2,1), so e comot if changed to 'less than 4'. Other points closer than 4, so dem stay. 2 5 4 2 1 4 4
y-m-44-06.s.s3.model.1: My points (2,1), (3,2), (0,1), (2,4) all less than 4 away from fountain, so dem stay even if change to 'less than'. Only boundary points exactly 4 away change. 2 1 3 2 0 1 2 4 4 4

y-m-44-04.title: When triangle formed by three lines disappears
y-m-44-04.topic: Positions of three lines (concurrent/parallel) and triangle conditions
y-m-44-04.goal: Review cases three lines cannot form triangle as info arrives; summarize for each k.
y-m-44-04.material: Lines l₁:y=x+1, l₂:y=−x+5, l₃:2x−y=k. k constant. Whether they enclose triangle depends on k. Read l₃ as 2x−y=k. [1 5 2]
y-m-44-04.prereq.1: Prerequisite: intersections of lines and triangle area from vertex coordinates.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.prompt: Information about lines revealed stepwise; choose reasonable view each time.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.hint.0: At each step note which triangle condition new fact changes.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether keep choice or change reason.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.info: Three lines slopes 1,−1,2 (k unknown); all distinct, no pair parallel. [1 1 5 1 2 2]
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: For any k, no two parallel. Does that guarantee triangle for every k?
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.after: Nonparallel is only one triangle condition. For some k all three may concur, so check.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: Since no lines parallel, triangle for every k.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Did you consider all three meeting at one point? Nonparallel can still fail triangle.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Depending k, triangle may fail, so check further.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You note nonparallel alone does not settle it; identify remaining cases.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: They are not parallel, so no triangle ever forms.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: If three different intersection points dey, those three points become triangle corners.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.info: l₁ and l₂ cross at (2, 3). Put (2, 3) into equation 2x−y=k for l₃, get 4−3=1.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: When k=1, three lines make triangle?
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.after: If k=1, l₃ pass through (2,3) too, so all three intersection points overlap at one point (2,3). Na one point remain, no triangle. 1 2 3 2 3
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Intersection (2,3) dey on all three lines, so three intersection points dey and triangle form 2 3
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Triangle form only if three intersection points different. Wetin happen if intersections of three lines join into one?
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: All three lines become same line, so no triangle
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Slopes of three lines different: 1, −1, 2, so dem no fit be same line.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Three lines meet at one point (2,3), so no triangle 2 3
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You point out say dem meet at one point, so all three intersections overlap as one.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.info: Now make k=3. Intersection of l₁ and l₃ na (4,5), l₂ and l₃ na (8/3, 7/3), and l₁ and l₂ na (2,3). These three points na triangle corners. 3 4 5 8 3 7 3 2 3
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: When k=3, wetin triangle area inside three lines be?
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.after: With corners (2,3), (4,5), (8/3,7/3), area na 4/3. Finding two-line intersection, checking if dem meet one point, and finding triangle area all connect. 2 3 4 5 8 3 7 3 4 3
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Dis value na two times another value. Check whether you forget halve when finding triangle area.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Put coordinates of three corners inside and calculate again. You fit choose wrong base and height.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You find area using coordinates of three corners.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.st.2.r.d: E look like product of coordinate differences without change. Triangle na half of rectangle.
y-m-44-04.s.s1.reflect: At first e easy think 'if dem no parallel, triangle go form'. How your judgment change each step? Which step make your confidence grow as information increase, and which step add conditions?
y-m-44-04.s.s2.prompt: Find all cases (how many?) where three lines no fit make triangle depending on k, and write reason in one or two sentences.

y-m-44-04.s.s2.model.1: Only case na when l₃ pass through intersection (2,3) of l₁ and l₂, meaning k=1. Then three lines meet at one point and no triangle form. For any other k, three intersections different. 2 3 1
